# The Problem

## Translations are typed by hand

A module holds one YAML file per help page, each string's `original` next to its `translation`, with live values kept as `{ISEXPR_n}` placeholders. rdlocal serves these files; it doesn't help you write them. Measured with `tools::Rd_db()`, the translatable help text is about 1 million characters for `base` (446 topics), 0.7 million for `stats`, 0.4 million for `utils` and 0.13 million for `MASS`. That's roughly 170,000 words for `base` alone, per language.

And rdlocal has contributors beyond me: during the R Project Sprint 2026 (1 to 3 September), where rdlocal was a user-testing task ([sprint #16](https://github.com/r-devel/r-project-sprint-2026/issues/16)), five people opened six pull requests on it.

## Why plain machine translation breaks help pages

It sounds like a translation task. It mostly isn't. This is `mean()`'s `x` argument in Elio's example module [base.es](https://github.com/eliocamp/base.es):

```
an \R{} object.  Currently there are methods for
    numeric/logical vectors and \link[=Dates]{date},
    \link{date-time} and \link{time interval} objects.  Complex vectors
    are allowed for \code{trim = 0}, only.
```

A correct translation changes the link text (`date`) but keeps the target (`=Dates`), leaves `\code{trim = 0}` and `\R{}` alone, and keeps every `{ISEXPR_n}` placeholder exactly once. Bare links are harder: the human Spanish translation there turns `\link{date-time}` into `\link[=date-time]{fecha-tiempo}`, adding a target so the link still resolves. Miss any of this and rdlocal can't match or re-parse the page, so the reader quietly gets English or a broken page.

## The review gap

R's own messages are translated on [Weblate](https://translate.rx.studio/), where bulk machine translation goes in as "needing edit" and isn't used until a translator reviews it ([r-dev-day #66](https://github.com/r-devel/r-dev-day/issues/66)). Modules have no working route there: an older `.po` workflow ([rdlocal #26](https://github.com/eliocamp/rdlocal/pull/26)) has been open since 2024 and predates the placeholders. Heather Turner opened that task as [sprint #17](https://github.com/r-devel/r-project-sprint-2026/issues/17), and Ashish Tiwari has posted a YAML to PO proof of concept on it.

## Existing work

| Tool | What it does | Gap |
|:--------------|:--------------------|:---------------------------|
| [lang](https://github.com/mlverse/lang) (Posit) | Live LLM translation of help, per user, cached locally | Not reviewed or shared; no rdlocal placeholders. Its README: "only a human curated translation will be the best solution" |
| [babeldown](https://docs.ropensci.org/babeldown/) (rOpenSci, ISC 2022-2) | DeepL for Markdown/Quarto, with glossaries | No Rd; babelrd follows its approach |
| [deeplr](https://cran.r-project.org/package=deeplr) | DeepL API wrapper | No Rd handling |

This builds on ISC grants for rhelpi18n (2023-2), babeldown (2022-2) and the [Consistent Translations Glossary](https://github.com/r-devel/glossary) (2025-2). It contributes to two items on the [Multilingual Documentation Working Group's plan](https://github.com/RConsortium/multilingual-documentation-wg): *"Keep translations up-to-date"* and *"Transform between formats accepted by existing translation services"*. No changes to R itself are proposed.
